# Thunder UI - AI Agent Instructions

Thunder UI is a React + Vite dashboard boilerplate for Thunder Framework. It reads your
backend's schemas through a generated `thunder-sdk` and builds navigation, list pages and forms
for every module automatically — and beyond that it is **a normal React app** you can build
anything in.

Because every generated screen comes from that SDK, a backend change only reaches the UI once
the SDK is rebuilt. See [Two Kinds of Update](#two-kinds-of-update).

## Upstream Context

- [Thunder Framework llms.txt](https://thunder.huruftech.com/llms.txt): the backend this UI is
  generated from — routers, `createCRUD`, schemas, and the `generate:app` task.
- [React docs](https://react.dev/): React 19 is the runtime.
- [Vite docs](https://vite.dev/): build tool, `import.meta.env`, modes.
- [Tailwind CSS v4](https://tailwindcss.com/docs): CSS-first config via `@theme`.
- [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/): headless primitives under the shadcn/ui components.
- [react-hook-form](https://react-hook-form.com/): form state for generated forms.
- [React Router](https://reactrouter.com/): `createBrowserRouter` data router.
- [Capacitor](https://capacitorjs.com/docs): the Android/iOS build.
- [ImageKit](https://imagekit.io/docs): upload and image transformation.

**Provenance.** Verified against the `thunder-ui` repository at commit `641ed47` on 2026-10-06.
Figures were measured, not estimated.

## Ground Rules For This File

1. **Treat this file as the boundary of what is known.** Do not state anything about Thunder UI
   that is not here, and do not infer behaviour from how similar tools work.
2. [Verify With The Framework Team](#verify-with-the-framework-team) lists facts that live in
   the framework's own tooling and could not be determined from this repository. Do not invent
   them.
3. File paths, type names and environment variable names are exact. Copy them verbatim.

---

## Project Structure

Inside a Thunder Framework project the app lives at `public/app/`, and the SDK it links to at
`public/www/sdk@<version>/`.

```
public/app/                # ← the generated Thunder UI app
├── src/
│   ├── core/              # FRAMEWORK INTERNALS (DO NOT MODIFY)
│   │   ├── router.tsx     # builds every route from SDK metadata
│   │   ├── protected.tsx  # auth gate (OIDC or cookie session)
│   │   ├── types.ts       # the override contracts
│   │   ├── crud/          # ListPage, FormPage, ViewPage, filters, field renderers
│   │   ├── layouts/       # navbar | sidebar | mobile | native + registry.ts
│   │   ├── custom/        # composite components (RefSelect, Datatable, …)
│   │   ├── lib/           # jsonSchemaToFields, utils, features, constants
│   │   ├── locals/        # Thunder UI's own translations
│   │   ├── pages/         # built-in pages (overview, wallet, users, notifications)
│   │   └── styles/        # mechanics only: keyframes, utilities, fonts
│   │
│   ├── overrides/         # Extension points — replace generated screens
│   │   ├── crud/{lists,cards,forms,views}.tsx
│   │   ├── icons.tsx
│   │   ├── layouts.ts
│   │   └── routes.tsx
│   │
│   ├── pages/             # YOUR pages
│   ├── components/        # YOUR components + the shadcn/ui primitives
│   ├── hooks/, lib/       # YOUR hooks and helpers
│   ├── locals/            # YOUR translations (merged over core's)
│   ├── index.css          # YOUR theme tokens
│   ├── App.tsx            # route tree + layout wiring
│   ├── main.tsx           # app entry
│   └── i18n.ts            # i18next setup
│
├── android/, ios/         # Capacitor native projects
├── www/                   # build output (gitignored; produced by the build)
├── .env, .env.example     # environment
└── capacitor.config.ts
```

### Critical: Never Edit `src/core/`

`src/core/` is managed by Thunder UI and is **overwritten** when the developer runs:

```bash
deno task generate:app --forceSync
```

That command replaces `src/core/` wholesale with the latest Thunder UI and leaves everything
else untouched. It is how fixes and security patches reach an existing project without
discarding the developer's work. Any manual change inside `src/core/` **will be lost — every
time, with no warning and no prompt.**

> The ONLY time editing `src/core/` is acceptable is while experimenting or debugging locally.
> Treat such edits as throwaway.

**Build on top instead:**

- Add pages in `src/pages/`, components in `src/components/`, helpers in `src/lib/`.
- Register replacements for generated screens in `src/overrides/`.
- Wrap or compose core utilities in your own modules.

Everything outside `src/core/` is yours and survives every update.

---

## It Is Still a Normal React App

**Do not present Thunder UI as a system you can only use through its CRUD generator.** The
generator removes the repetitive part — one list page and one form per backend module — and
nothing more. The rest is an ordinary React + Vite application.

Developers are free to:

- Add pages with any content, generated or hand-written, CRUD-related or not.
- Add components, hooks, contexts and utilities anywhere outside `src/core/`.
- Install any npm dependency and use it normally.
- Call the SDK directly, call their own endpoints, or call a third-party API.
- Build features with no backend module behind them at all — a dashboard, a report, a wizard,
  a landing page.
- Add as many layouts/themes as they want and switch between them.
- Restyle everything through theme tokens, or ignore the tokens and write their own CSS.

```tsx
// src/pages/analytics.tsx — a plain React page, nothing schema-driven about it
import { useEffect, useState } from "react"
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader } from "@/components/ui/card"

export default function Analytics() {
  const [data, setData] = useState<number[]>([])

  useEffect(() => {
    fetch("/analytics/api/daily")
      .then((r) => r.json())
      .then(setData)
  }, [])

  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>Daily signups</CardHeader>
      <CardContent>{data.length} days loaded</CardContent>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

```tsx
// src/overrides/routes.tsx — make it reachable
import { IconChartBar } from "@tabler/icons-react"
import Analytics from "@/pages/analytics"
import type { TRoutesOverride } from "@/core/types"

export const routes: TRoutesOverride = {
  analytics: { name: "Analytics", icon: IconChartBar, Component: Analytics },
}
```

The only hard rule is the one above: don't edit `src/core/`.

---

## Installation

Thunder UI is not installed with a package manager. It is generated into a Thunder Framework
project, from that project's root:

```bash
deno task generate:app
```

`--forceSync` is the only flag.

What it does:

1. Clones Thunder UI into **`public/app/`** in the framework project.
2. Generates an SDK from the backend's routes and schemas into **`public/www/sdk@<version>/`**.
3. Rewrites the app's `package.json` to point `thunder-sdk` at that SDK:
   ```jsonc
   "thunder-sdk": "file:///../www/sdk@<latest-version>/npm"
   ```
4. Runs the install and the first build for you.
5. The app then derives its navigation and CRUD screens from that SDK.

So the dependency is a **local `file:` link to a versioned directory on the backend**, not a
package downloaded from a registry.

> The `thunder-sdk` entry committed in this repository points at a published tarball
> (`https://…/sdk@x.y.z/package.tgz`). That is only the standalone default so the boilerplate
> can be built on its own — `generate:app` replaces it with the `file:` link above.

The web build outputs to `www/` inside the app directory and is served under the base path
`/app` (`vite.config.ts` sets `build.outDir: "./www"`; the build passes `--base=/app`). `www/`
is **gitignored** — it is a build artifact, produced by `generate:app` on install and by
`npm run build` afterwards. The `.env` files, by contrast, are committed deliberately.

### Two Kinds of Update

**Do not conflate these.** It is the distinction developers get wrong most often — two
independent things can go stale, with two different commands:

| What changed | What to run | What it refreshes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Your backend** — a schema, or a route's shape | `deno task generate:sdk` then rebuild | the generated screens: columns, filters, form fields |
| **Thunder UI itself** — a fix or new feature upstream | `deno task generate:app --forceSync` | `src/core/` |

#### After changing a backend schema or route

The UI reads everything from the generated SDK, so a backend change is invisible until the SDK
is rebuilt:

```bash
# 1. Rebuild the SDK from the current routes and schemas
deno task generate:sdk -v <latest-version> --overwrite
```

Then pick up the new SDK in the app, either way:

```bash
# 2a. relinks package.json to the new SDK version, reinstalls and rebuilds
deno task generate:app --forceSync

# 2b. or, from public/app, just rebuild
npm run build
```

Choose by whether the **version changed**: the `thunder-sdk` entry names a specific
`sdk@<version>` directory, so a new version needs `generate:app` to rewrite that link.
Overwriting the same version in place leaves the link valid, and a rebuild is enough.

Nothing in `src/` needs editing. New modules appear in navigation on their own, new properties
appear as columns and form fields, and a changed `fieldHint` or `ref` changes the control that
renders — all from the schema.

> **Symptom to recognise:** a developer says they added a field (or a whole module) on the
> backend and "Thunder UI isn't showing it". The answer is almost always that the SDK has not
> been regenerated.

#### Updating Thunder UI itself

```bash
deno task generate:app --forceSync
```

Replaces `src/core/` with the latest Thunder UI, relinks the SDK, reinstalls and rebuilds.
Everything outside `src/core/` is left alone.

> **It replaces `src/core/` unconditionally and does not warn.** Any edit inside that directory
> is lost, every time. Commit your own work first so the resulting diff is reviewable.

---

## How CRUD Screens Are Generated

`src/core/router.tsx` builds the route tree at module load **from the installed SDK** — so a
backend module that does not appear here is usually a stale SDK, not a routing problem. See
[Two Kinds of Update](#two-kinds-of-update).

1. **Module names** come from `ThunderSDK.getModuleNames()`, plus any key in
   `src/overrides/routes.tsx` that is not an SDK group and is not a built-in route key.
2. **Per module**, if an override exists without `merge: true`, it replaces the generated route
   entirely. Otherwise a route is generated and the override is spread over it, so `merge: true`
   changes `name`/`icon`/`priority` while keeping the generated children.
3. **Grouping** uses `ThunderSDK.getGroup(name)` — the `.group("Label")` on the backend router,
   deliberately shared across several route files (see
   [Route level](#route-level-the-router-file)). Each group becomes a parent route whose path is the group name lowercased with
   whitespace replaced by dashes. A group's index redirects to its first visible child.
4. **Visibility** requires `ThunderSDK.isPermitted(name, "get")` or
   `isPermitted(name, "create")`, and the override's `display` must allow it. A group shows only
   if a child is visible.
5. **Built-ins** `overview`, `wallet` and `notifications` are prepended and replaceable by name.

### Generated children per module

| Child path | Component | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| index | `ListPage`, or the `lists` override | always |
| `form`, `form/:id` | `FormPage` | only if the module has `create` or `update` |
| `:id` | `ViewPage` | always |

### URL shape

| URL | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | redirects to `/select-tenant` |
| `/select-tenant` | tenant picker |
| `/:tenant/overview` | landing page |
| `/:tenant/<group>/<module>` | list |
| `/:tenant/<group>/<module>/form` | create |
| `/:tenant/<group>/<module>/form/:id` | edit |
| `/:tenant/<group>/<module>/:id` | detail |

The `:tenant` segment is pushed into the SDK via `ThunderSDK.plugins.essentials.setTenant()`.

### TRouteObject

```ts
type TRouteObject = {
  name?: string                        // nav label; passed through t()
  priority?: number | (() => number)   // ascending; ties keep declaration order
  group?: string
  icon?: TablerIcon
  display?: boolean | (() => boolean)
  children?: TRouteObject[]
  button?: React.ComponentType         // rendered beside the nav entry
} & RouteObject
```

---

## Controlling the UI From the Backend Schema

This is the part that ties the two projects together, and the part a developer is most likely to
be looking for.

Thunder UI never guesses at layout. **The form's grouping, labels, control types, help text and
which columns are filterable are all declared on the backend**, as zod `.meta()` on the schema
fields. Those keys have no meaning to the database or to validation — they exist only to shape
the generated UI, and they travel to the frontend inside the JSON Schema the SDK carries.

It happens at two levels: the **router file** decides the module's name, its navigation group
and which pages exist; the **schema fields** decide the form's layout and controls.

A field's plain zod type already decides a lot (see [What plain zod already
implies](#what-plain-zod-already-implies)); `.meta()` is for everything zod cannot express.

### Route level: the router file

A backend route file becomes one module in the UI. Two things on it matter:

```ts
// routes/rosters.ts  (Thunder Framework — backend)
import { Router } from "@/core/http/router.ts";
import { createCRUD } from "@/core/utils/createCRUD.ts";
import {
  rosterInputSchema,
  rosterModel,
  rosterSchema,
} from "@/schemas/hr/roster.ts";
import { withTenant } from "@plugins/Huruf-Tech/thunder-core/utils/withTenant.ts";

export default new Router("/api", function rosters(router) {
  createCRUD({
    router,
    schema: rosterSchema,             // → list columns, filters, detail
    insertSchema: rosterInputSchema,  // → the create form
    model: rosterModel,
  }, {
    isolationFields: async (req, action) => {
      const { tenant, user } = await withTenant(req);

      if (action === "create") {
        return { tenant: tenant._id, createdBy: user._id };
      }

      return { tenant: tenant._id };
    },
  });
}).group("HR Admin");               // → the UI's navigation group
```

**The router's name is the module name.** `function rosters(router)` — matching the filename by
convention — is the key you use everywhere in the UI: `overrides/crud/cards.tsx`,
`overrides/routes.tsx`, `<ListPage name="rosters" />`.

Navigation **order** is not set here. `priority` is a frontend-only concern — see
[Reordering modules and groups](#reordering-modules-and-groups).

**`.group("Label")` is what groups routes in the navigation.** It is a *shared label*, reused
deliberately across several route files — every file tagged `.group("HR Admin")` lands in one
`HR Admin` group in the sidebar, with one parent route:

```
routes/rosters.ts           .group("HR Admin")  ─┐
routes/overtimePolicies.ts  .group("HR Admin")  ─┼─→  /:tenant/hr-admin/...
routes/leavePolicies.ts     .group("HR Admin")  ─┘
```

The group's URL segment is the label lowercased with whitespace replaced by dashes, so
`.group("HR Admin")` serves at `/:tenant/hr-admin/<module>`. A module with no `.group()` falls
into a group literally named `Other`.

### The three schemas and what each one drives

`createCRUD` takes up to three schemas, and the UI uses a different one per surface:

| `createCRUD` option | Used for | UI surface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | the full document shape | list columns, the filter menu, and the `output` intent |
| `insertSchema` | the create payload | the **create** form (`/form`) |
| `updateSchema` | the update payload | the **edit** form (`/form/:id`) |

Resolution is tolerant, so you only declare what differs:

| Intent | Falls back through |
| --- | --- |
| create | `insertSchema` → `schema` |
| edit | `updateSchema` → `insertSchema` → `schema` |
| list / detail | `schema` |

So a module with only `schema` still gets working create and edit forms. Supplying
`insertSchema` keeps server-generated fields (`_id`, `createdAt`, `tenant`) out of the form, and
supplying `updateSchema` lets you narrow what is editable after creation:

```ts
createCRUD({
  router,
  schema: rosterSchema,
  insertSchema: rosterInputSchema,
  updateSchema: rosterInputSchema.pick({ name: true }),  // only the name is editable
  model: rosterModel,
});
```

### Disabled operations remove pages

The UI generates pages from the endpoints the SDK actually exposes:

- No `create` **and** no `update` on the module → **no form route at all**.
- No `del` → the delete action disappears from the list page's action bar.

So disabling an endpoint on the backend (`createCRUD(..., { disable: { del: true } })`) removes
the corresponding UI, with nothing to change in the frontend.

Fields injected by `isolationFields` — `tenant`, `createdBy` and similar — are set server-side
and normally absent from `insertSchema`, so they never appear as form inputs. That is the
intended arrangement: keep them out of the insert schema and the UI will not ask for them.

### Field level: a worked schema

Excerpt from a real employee schema, showing every technique in one place:

```ts
// schemas/employee.ts  (Thunder Framework — backend)
export const employeeInputSchema = z.object({
  // pick a specific control
  avatar: z.url().meta({ fieldHint: "avatar" }).optional(),

  // three fields on one row: the GROUP's classes go on its FIRST field
  fname: z.string().max(50).meta({
    group: "fullName",
    groupClassName: "grid grid-cols-2 gap-4",
    label: "First Name",
  }),
  mname: z.string().max(50).optional().meta({
    group: "fullName",
    label: "Middle Name",
  }),
  lname: z.string().max(50).optional().meta({
    group: "fullName",
    className: "col-span-2",          // this one field spans the grid
    label: "Last Name",
  }),

  // enum + filterable
  gender: z.enum(Gender).optional().meta({ group: "bio", canFilter: true }),

  // a reference, rendered as a type-ahead over the users module
  user: $objectId.meta({
    ref: "users",
    refLabel: ["name", "email"],
    fieldHint: "autocomplete",
  }).optional(),

  // long text becomes a textarea automatically (maxLength > 100)
  address_1: z.string().max(300).optional().meta({
    group: "address",
    groupClassName: "grid grid-cols-2 gap-4",
    className: "col-span-2",
  }),

  // an array of objects → a repeatable field group with add/remove
  identity: z.array(
    z.object({
      kind: z.enum(IdentityKind),
      description: z.optional(z.string().max(150)),
      documents: z.array(
        z.url().meta({ label: "Identity documents", fieldHint: "upload" }),
      ).optional(),
    }),
  ).meta({
    label: "Identify your employee",
    description: "A proof of identity is a must in order to proceed",
  }),

  // a nested object → its own fieldset, with its own internal grouping
  bankDetails: z.object({
    bankName: z.string().max(100).meta({
      group: "bankName",
      groupClassName: "grid grid-cols-2 gap-4",
    }),
    accountName: z.string().max(50).meta({ group: "bankName" }),
    accountNumber: z.string().max(120).optional(),
  }).meta({
    label: "Bank Details",
    description: "How is this employee going to be paid?",
  }).optional(),

  // `.describe()` is the same as `.meta({ description })`
  contract: z.object({
    kind: z.enum(ContractKind).meta({ label: "Contract Kind" }),
    joinedAt: z.coerce.date().describe("Start the payroll period").meta({
      group: "dates",
      groupClassName: "grid grid-cols-2 gap-4",
      canFilter: true,
    }),
    department: $objectId.meta({ ref: "departments" }).meta({
      group: "work",
      canFilter: true,
    }),
  }).optional(),
})
```

> `.meta()` can be chained — `z.coerce.date().meta({ label }).optional().meta({ group })` merges
> both objects. This is why you often see one `.meta()` on the inner type (for `ref`) and
> another after `.optional()` (for layout).

### The metadata keys

| Key | Put it on | Effect in Thunder UI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | any field, object, array | The visible label. On an object or array it becomes the fieldset legend. Passed through `t()`. |
| `description` (or `.describe()`) | any field, object, array | Help text under the field, or under a fieldset's legend. Passed through `t()`. |
| `group` | a field | Renders this field in the same row/grid as its neighbours carrying the same value. See below. |
| `groupClassName` | the **first** field of a group | Tailwind classes for the group container, e.g. `"grid grid-cols-2 gap-4"`. |
| `groupStyle` | the **first** field of a group | Inline styles for the group container. |
| `className` | a field | Tailwind classes for that one field, e.g. `"col-span-2"` to span a grid. |
| `style` | a field | Inline styles for that one field. |
| `fieldHint` | a field | Picks a specific control. See the [`fieldHint` table](#fieldhint). |
| `canFilter` | a field | **Required** for the field to appear in the list page's filter menu. |
| `ref` | an ObjectId field | Module this field references; renders a searchable picker. |
| `refLabel` | a `ref` field | Property or properties to display, e.g. `["fname", "lname"]`. |
| `refValue` | a `ref` field | Property to submit. Defaults to `_id`. |
| `refFilters` | a `ref` field | Filters applied when querying the referenced module. |
| `example` | a field | Placeholder text. |
| `requirementKey` | a field | Render only when the watched field's value equals this field's name. |
| `fileType`, `fileSize` | an upload field | Accepted types and max size. |
| `filterSchema` | an object field | Schema name for `fieldHint: "filters"`. |
| `queryValue`, `ignoreQueryValue` | a field | Prefill from a URL query parameter, or opt out of it. |

Any other key on a schema property is carried through to the field object untouched, so a custom
override component can read whatever it likes.

### Grouping: two rules that surprise people

**1. Grouping is by *consecutive* fields.** Thunder UI walks the properties in order and starts a
new group each time the `group` value changes. Two blocks with the same `group` name separated by
a differently-grouped field become **two separate groups** — the name is not an identifier.
Declare grouped fields next to each other in the schema.

```ts
// ✅ one row of three
fname: …meta({ group: "fullName", groupClassName: "grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" }),
mname: …meta({ group: "fullName" }),
lname: …meta({ group: "fullName" }),

// ❌ two separate "fullName" groups, because `email` interrupts
fname: …meta({ group: "fullName" }),
email: …,
lname: …meta({ group: "fullName" }),
```

**2. The group's own classes come from its first field.** `groupClassName` and `groupStyle` are
read off `fields[0]` of each group, so set them on the first member only. Setting them on a later
member has no effect.

Fields with no `group` are rendered one per row.

### `canFilter` is opt-in

A field does **not** appear in the list page's filter menu unless it carries
`canFilter: true`. The menu additionally excludes `url`, `hidden`, `object` and `array` fields,
so `canFilter` on those does nothing.

This is the single most commonly missed key: the field shows up as a table column and a form
input regardless, but is unfilterable until the backend says otherwise.

### What plain zod already implies

Most of the UI follows from the type alone — reach for `.meta()` only when you need to override
one of these:

| On the backend | In Thunder UI |
| --- | --- |
| `.optional()` | field is not required; label gets an "(optional)" suffix |
| required (no `.optional()`) | field is required, with a generated message |
| `z.string().max(n)` where `n <= 100` | single-line input, with `maxLength` validation |
| `z.string().max(n)` where `n > 100`, or no `max` | **textarea** |
| `z.string().min(n)` | `minLength` validation |
| `z.number().min()/.max()` | number input with range validation |
| `z.boolean()` | switch |
| `z.enum(X)` | dropdown (multiselect when inside an array) |
| `z.url()` | url input — or an uploader with `fieldHint` |
| `z.email()` | email input |
| `z.e164()` | international phone input |
| `z.coerce.date()` | date input (add `fieldHint: "datetime-local"` for a time too) |
| `z.array(z.string())` | tag input |
| `z.array(z.object({…}))` | repeatable field group with add/remove |
| `z.object({…})` | nested fieldset |
| `z.record(…)` | JSON textarea |
| `.default(v)` | pre-filled value |
| `$objectId.meta({ ref })` | searchable reference picker |
| `z.literal(v)` / a `const` | hidden, submitted as that value |
| `.regex(...)` | `pattern` validation |

A field's `required` state comes from the parent object's `required` list, which zod derives from
`.optional()`. Nothing in the UI needs to be told about it.

### After editing a schema

The UI reads all of this from the generated SDK, so none of it takes effect until the SDK is
rebuilt — see [Two Kinds of Update](#two-kinds-of-update).

---

## Schema to Form Fields

`src/core/crud/metadata.ts` exports `fieldsFromModuleMetadata(metadata, opts)`, which picks the
schema by intent and converts it with `JSONSchemaToFields.toFields`:

| Intent | Schema resolution |
| --- | --- |
| `insert` | `crud.insertSchema ?? crud.schema` |
| `update` | `crud.updateSchema ?? crud.insertSchema ?? crud.schema` |
| `output` | `crud.schema` |

The function is **total** — it always returns `TField[]` and never rejects. A module that exposes
`create`/`update` without a schema yields an empty array and the form shows an empty state.

The [worked schema](#field-level-a-worked-schema) above exercises most of this.

### JSON Schema support matrix

| Construct | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `object` with `properties` | nested field group, arbitrarily deep |
| `array` of objects | repeatable group (`orders.0.lines.0.sku`) |
| `array` of scalars | tag input (`multi`) |
| `array` of arrays of scalars | per-row tag input |
| `required` | propagates, including inside array items |
| `enum` | dropdown (strings or numbers) |
| `format`: `date`, `date-time`, `email`, `uri`, `e164` | date / date / email / url / phone |
| `$ref` / `$defs` | resolved, including recursive refs |
| `allOf` | merged into the host schema |
| `oneOf` / `anyOf` | branches merged into one object; a `const` discriminator becomes an enum |
| `type: ["string","null"]` | resolves to the non-null type |
| `default` | becomes the field's initial value |
| `const` | submitted, rendered hidden |
| `additionalProperties` | JSON textarea |
| `prefixItems` | sibling fields `name.0`, `name.1` |

**Default rule:** a property is **optional** unless its parent lists it in `required`.

Unsupported constructs degrade to a text input **and** emit a one-time `console.warn`. Set
`JSONSchemaToFields.silent = true` to suppress those.

### Field type to control

| Field | Control |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `maxLength` absent or > 100 | textarea |
| `text`, `maxLength` ≤ 100 | single-line input |
| `number` | number input |
| `boolean` | switch |
| `date` | date input |
| `email` / `url` | input with the matching type |
| `phone` | international phone input (lazy-loaded) |
| `hidden` | not rendered; still registered if it has `const` |
| `enum` present | dropdown, or multiselect when `multi` |
| `ref` present | searchable, server-paginated picker |
| `array` of objects | repeatable group with add/remove |
| `object` | nested field group |
| any `multi` scalar | tag input |

### fieldHint

A schema property may carry `fieldHint` to pick a specific control:

| `fieldHint` | Applies to | Control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `avatar` | `url`, single | avatar uploader |
| `upload` | `url` | file table uploader (`fileType`, `fileSize`, `maxItems` honoured) |
| `markdown` | `text` | markdown editor (lazy-loaded) |
| `json` | `text` | JSON textarea; blocks invalid JSON |
| `autocomplete` | `enum` | type-ahead instead of a dropdown |
| `amount` | `number` | amount-styled number input |
| `datetime-local` | `date` | date + time input |
| `filters` | `object` | MongoDB filter builder; requires `filterSchema` |

### Reference fields

A field with `ref` renders a searchable, server-paginated picker that queries the referenced
module on demand — 25 per page, debounced search, every request abortable. This is what
Thunder's foreign-reference fields produce.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ref` | module name this field references |
| `refLabel` | `string \| string[]` — property/properties to display |
| `refValue` | property to submit (default `_id`) |
| `refFilters` | filters applied when querying the referenced module |

### TField

The shape the renderers consume. Any extra key on a JSON Schema property is carried through onto
the field, which is how the hints above work.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | field type above, or `"array"` / `"object"` |
| `name` | dotted path used as the form field name |
| `label`, `description` | passed through `t()` |
| `placeholder`, `example` | placeholder text |
| `optional` | `true` unless the parent requires it |
| `defaultValue` | from the schema's `default` |
| `multi` | scalar array → tag input |
| `enum` | `string[]` or `{ label, value }[]` |
| `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `pattern` | validation |
| `fieldHint` | see above |
| `const` | single legal value; submitted, not editable |
| `group` | consecutive fields sharing a group render in one `FieldGroup` |
| `groupClassName`, `groupStyle`, `className`, `style` | styling passthrough |
| `requirementKey` | render only when the watched field's value equals this field's name |
| `fileType`, `fileSize` | upload constraints |
| `queryValue`, `ignoreQueryValue` | prefill from a URL query parameter, or opt out |
| `fields` | child fields for `array` and `object` |

### Validation

`buildRules(field, t)` derives the react-hook-form rules from the schema: `required`, `pattern`,
`minLength`/`maxLength` for text, `min`/`max` for numbers, `minItems`/`maxItems` for arrays. All
messages go through `t()`.

Server-side messages surface automatically: an axios interceptor registered in `initThunder()`
raises one toast per entry in `error.response.data.messages`. Aborted requests never toast.

---

## Customization

### Replacing a generated screen

Everything in `src/overrides/` is a registry `src/core/` reads at startup. Keys are SDK module
names, group names, or built-in route keys.

```tsx
// src/overrides/crud/lists.tsx — replace a whole list page
export const lists: TListPagesOverride = { posts: PostList }
// props: TListPageProps = { group?: string; name: string }
```

```tsx
// src/overrides/crud/forms.tsx — replace a whole form (component takes no props)
export const forms: TFormsOverride = { posts: PostForm }

// src/overrides/crud/views.tsx — supply a detail page (no props, like forms)
export const views: TViewsOverride = { posts: PostDetail }

// src/overrides/icons.tsx — nav icon per module or group
export const icons: TIconsOverride = { posts: IconNotebook }

// src/overrides/layouts.ts — your own layouts, loaded on demand
export const layouts: TLayoutsOverride = { compact: () => import("@/layouts/compact") }
```

`src/overrides/crud/cards.tsx` and `src/overrides/routes.tsx` do the most work and are covered
in their own sections below.

A detail component takes **no props**. Read the record id from the route and fetch it however
you like — data loading is entirely yours:

```tsx
// src/pages/posts/PostDetail.tsx
import React from "react"
import { useParams } from "react-router"
import { ThunderSDK } from "thunder-sdk"

import { use } from "@/core/hooks/use"
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton"

export default function PostDetail() {
  const { id } = useParams<{ id: string }>()

  const request = React.useMemo(
    () =>
      ThunderSDK.useCaching(
        ["posts", id],
        async ({ signal }) =>
          (await ThunderSDK.posts.get({ signal, params: { id } })) as {
            results: unknown[]
          }
      ),
    [id]
  )

  const { data, isLoading } = use(request)
  const post = data?.results?.[0]

  if (isLoading) return <Skeleton className="h-40 w-full" />

  return <pre>{JSON.stringify(post, null, 2)}</pre>
}
```

`use()` (`@/core/hooks/use`) pairs with `ThunderSDK.useCaching` and gives you
`{ data, error, isLoading, refetch }`. A module `get` with `params: { id }` returns
`{ results: [record] }`.

When no view is registered for a module, its detail route goes to that module's edit form.

### Table vs card list

The two list views fetch differently, and the difference drives the choice between them:

| | Table (default) | Card view (an override) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fetching | the **whole collection**, in one request | one page at a time, `offset`/`limit` |
| Paging, sorting | client-side, owned by the table itself | server-side; core renders the pager below your component |
| Fetch trigger | automatic | **your component must call `fetcher()`** |

The table loads the full set on purpose: it then pages, sorts and filters client-side with no
further round trips. Card views take the server-paginated path instead, which is what you want
when the view should fetch incrementally.

### Card views

A card view replaces the table on a module's list page. Registering one adds a table/cards
toggle to the header and makes cards the default:

```tsx
// src/overrides/crud/cards.tsx
import type { TCardsOverride } from "@/core/types"
import JobsList from "@/pages/jobs/JobsList"

export const cards: TCardsOverride = { jobs: JobsList }
```

#### Critical: a card view must call `fetcher()`

In card mode the list page's fetch hooks are created with `manualTrigger: true`, so **nothing
is requested until your component asks for it.** Call `fetcher()` from an effect or your card
renders forever against an empty `data` array.

`fetcher(projection?, sorting?)` both triggers the request and, if you pass them, sets the
projection and sort for it. Projections matter here: a card usually needs a handful of fields,
not the whole document.

```tsx
React.useEffect(() => {
  fetcher(zodToMongoProjection(jobsSchema))
}, [fetcher])
```

`zodToMongoProjection` (from `@/core/lib/zodToMongoProjection`) walks a zod schema and returns
`{ field: 1 }` for every leaf, flattening nested objects to dot paths (`education.fieldOfStudy`)
and arrays without an index segment. Declaring the schema once gives you the projection *and* a
parser for the `unknown[]` you receive back.

#### The props

| Prop | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `data: unknown[]` | the records — parse them yourself |
| `isLoading` | first load; show a skeleton |
| `isRefetching` | a later load; usually a subtler indicator |
| `fetcher(projection?, sorting?)` | **trigger a fetch**, optionally setting projection and sort |
| `setProject(projection)` | change the projection without fetching |
| `setSort({ field: 1 \| -1 })` | change sort order; triggers a refetch |
| `setFilters(filters)` | set the SDK-level `filters` for the query |
| `setPage(index)` | **zero-based** page index |
| `selectedIds` | `_id`s currently selected |
| `toggleSelect(id?)` | toggle one row; with no argument, toggles the whole page |
| `name` | the module name, for cache keys or labels |

Selection is shared with the core action bar — call `toggleSelect` and the delete/edit bar at
the bottom of the page lights up with no extra work.

Pagination is rendered by the list page **below** your component, driven by the same
`page`/`pageSize` it passes into the query. You only need `setPage` if you want to drive paging
yourself, for example from an infinite scroller.

#### A worked example

```tsx
// src/pages/jobs/JobsList.tsx
import React from "react"
import z from "zod"
import { useNavigate } from "react-router"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { VirtuosoGrid } from "react-virtuoso"

import type { TCardProps } from "@/core/types"
import { zodToMongoProjection } from "@/core/lib/zodToMongoProjection"
import { Card, CardContent } from "@/components/ui/card"
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/ui/checkbox"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { Badge } from "@/components/ui/badge"
import { Empty, EmptyHeader, EmptyTitle } from "@/components/ui/empty"

// Declared once: drives the projection AND parses the response.
const jobsSchema = z.object({
  _id: z.string(),
  title: z.string(),
  salary: z.number().optional(),
  vacancies: z.number().optional(),
  applicationDeadline: z.union([z.string(), z.date()]).optional(),
  positionDetails: z
    .object({ position: z.string(), jobType: z.string() })
    .optional(),
  education: z.object({ highestQualification: z.string() }),
})

export default function JobsList({
  data,
  isLoading,
  fetcher,
  setSort,
  setFilters,
  toggleSelect,
  selectedIds = [],
}: TCardProps) {
  const { t, i18n } = useTranslation()
  const navigate = useNavigate()
  const [scrollParent, setScrollParent] = React.useState<HTMLDivElement | null>(null)

  // REQUIRED: card mode does not fetch on its own.
  React.useEffect(() => {
    fetcher(zodToMongoProjection(jobsSchema))
  }, [fetcher])

  // `data` is `unknown[]`; parse it with the same schema.
  const jobs = React.useMemo(
    () => (Array.isArray(data) ? jobsSchema.array().parse(data) : []),
    [data]
  )

  return (
    <div
      ref={setScrollParent}
      className="flex h-full min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col overflow-y-auto"
    >
      {/* Your own controls can drive the query directly. */}
      <div className="flex gap-2 p-2">
        <Button
          size="sm"
          variant="outline"
          onClick={() => setSort({ applicationDeadline: 1 })}
        >
          {t("Closing soonest")}
        </Button>
        <Button
          size="sm"
          variant="outline"
          onClick={() => setFilters({ isOpen: true })}
        >
          {t("Open only")}
        </Button>
      </div>

      {isLoading ? (
        <JobsListSkeleton />
      ) : jobs.length === 0 ? (
        <Empty className="min-h-[50vh]">
          <EmptyHeader>
            <EmptyTitle>{t("No jobs found")}</EmptyTitle>
          </EmptyHeader>
        </Empty>
      ) : (
        <VirtuosoGrid
          customScrollParent={scrollParent ?? undefined}
          computeItemKey={(_, job) => job._id}
          data={jobs}
          listClassName="grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-3"
          itemContent={(_, job) => {
            const position = job.positionDetails?.position ?? job.title
            const deadline = job.applicationDeadline
              ? new Date(job.applicationDeadline).toLocaleDateString(i18n.language)
              : null

            return (
              <Card className="flex h-full flex-col gap-3 p-4">
                <CardContent className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-3 p-0">
                  <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-3">
                    {/* Selection feeds the core action bar. */}
                    <Checkbox
                      checked={selectedIds.includes(job._id)}
                      onCheckedChange={() => toggleSelect(job._id)}
                      onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
                    />
                    {job.vacancies ? (
                      <Badge variant="secondary">
                        {t("{{count}} openings", { count: job.vacancies })}
                      </Badge>
                    ) : null}
                  </div>

                  <h3 className="line-clamp-1 text-lg font-semibold">{position}</h3>

                  {deadline && (
                    <small className="text-muted-foreground">
                      {t("Deadline")}: {deadline}
                    </small>
                  )}

                  <Button
                    size="sm"
                    className="mt-auto"
                    // `state.name` becomes the trailing breadcrumb on the detail page.
                    onClick={() => navigate(`./${job._id}`, { state: { name: position } })}
                  >
                    {t("Details")}
                  </Button>
                </CardContent>
              </Card>
            )
          }}
        />
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

Notes on the example worth repeating in prose:

- **Virtualise long lists.** `react-virtuoso` is already a dependency. Pass
  `customScrollParent` so the card view scrolls inside the page shell rather than the window.
- **`state: { name }` on navigate** sets the detail page's trailing breadcrumb — the breadcrumb
  reads `location.state.name`. `useBreadcrumbTitle()` does the same thing from inside a page.
- Driving the query from your own UI is just calling `setSort`, `setFilters` or `setProject`;
  each triggers a refetch through the same cached query the table uses.

### Routes: hiding, reordering and replacing

`src/overrides/routes.tsx` is the single most used extension point. Keys are **SDK module
names**, **group names** (as the SDK reports them, usually capitalised), or the built-in keys
`overview`, `wallet`, `notifications`.

#### The one rule that governs everything here

| Form | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `key: { … }` | **Replaces** the generated route entirely. Only what you write exists. |
| `key: { merge: true, … }` | **Merges** over the generated route. Keeps its `path`, `Component` and generated children. |

Everything below follows from that.

#### Hiding a module

Two different outcomes, and the difference matters:

```tsx
// Remove it completely — the list/form/detail pages stop existing.
// No `merge`, so `{ display: false }` *becomes* the whole route.
tenants: { display: false },
apiKeys: { display: false },
accessControl: { display: false },

// Keep the pages reachable by URL, just hide them from navigation.
// Use this for screens you link to yourself from somewhere else.
attributeValues: { merge: true, display: false },
stores: { merge: true, display: false },
```

#### Gating visibility on a permission

`display` may be a function, re-evaluated whenever navigation renders. Any permission works —
including a different module's, which is how you hide a screen behind the permission that
actually guards its data:

```tsx
products: { merge: true, display: () => ThunderSDK.isPermitted(ThunderSDK.products.update) },
brands:   { merge: true, display: () => ThunderSDK.isPermitted(ThunderSDK.brands.update) },

// gated by a *different* module's permission
categories: {
  merge: true,
  display: () => ThunderSDK.isPermitted(ThunderSDK.manageOrders.get),
},
```

#### Reordering modules and groups

`priority` sorts ascending; ties keep declaration order. **It can only be set here** — the
backend has no say in navigation order. Group keys work exactly like module keys:

```tsx
orders:             { merge: true, priority: 0 },
orderSubscriptions: { merge: true, priority: 1 },

// group-level overrides — keyed by the group name
Management: { merge: true, priority: 1 },
Admin:      { merge: true, priority: 4 },
Orders:     { merge: true, priority: 4 },
```

> A group's own `display` is ANDed with "has at least one visible child", so a group
> disappears automatically once everything inside it is hidden. You do not need to hide the
> group as well.

#### Adding your own page into an existing group

Set `group` to the group you want it to appear under. The group does not have to come from the
SDK — naming a new one creates it:

```tsx
refundableOrders: {
  name: "Refundable Orders",
  path: "refundableOrders",
  group: "Management",                     // joins an existing group
  icon: IconCreditCardRefund,
  display: () => ThunderSDK.isPermitted(ThunderSDK.manageOrders.refundable),
  Component: RefundableOrders,
},

manageCareers: {
  name: "Manage Careers",
  path: "manageCareers",
  group: "Careers",                        // creates a new group
  icon: IconDeviceDesktopCog,
  display: () => ThunderSDK.isPermitted(ThunderSDK.manageCareers.get),
  Component: ManageCareers,
},
```

> Routes are grouped by `group ?? "Other"`. A route with no `group` therefore lands in a group
> literally named **Other** — which is visible if that route is. Always set `group` on a custom
> route unless you actually want that. (This is also why a bare `{ display: false }` is safe:
> with nothing visible inside it, the `Other` group hides itself.)

#### Hidden deep-linked routes

A route with `display: false` is reachable by URL but absent from navigation — the usual shape
for a detail page you link to from a list. `path` can be several segments with parameters:

```tsx
manageCareerDetail: {
  path: "manageCareers/:id",
  group: "Careers",
  display: false,
  Component: ManageCareerDetail,
},

orderSubscriptionsTriggers: {
  path: "orderSubscriptions/:subscriptionId/triggers/:triggerId",
  group: "Orders",
  display: false,
  Component: SubscriptionTriggerDetailView,
},
```

#### Rebuilding the children yourself

Because an override without `merge` replaces the route outright, you can declare the children
by hand — and still reuse the generated pages. `ListPage`, `ViewPage` and `FormPage` are
exported from core and take `group` and `name`, so you keep the schema-driven screens while
changing the URL layout. Here the module is relabelled and its `form` segment becomes `apply`:

```tsx
import { Outlet } from "react-router"
import { ListPage } from "@/core/crud/ListPage.tsx"
import { ViewPage } from "@/core/crud/ViewPage.tsx"
import { FormPage } from "@/core/crud/FormPage.tsx"

careers: {
  name: "Applications",                    // nav label differs from the module name
  path: "careers",
  group: "Careers",
  icon: IconDeviceDesktopCog,
  display: () => ThunderSDK.isPermitted(ThunderSDK.careers.get),
  Component: () => <Outlet />,             // parent renders its children
  children: [
    {
      index: true,
      display: false,
      Component: () => <ListPage group="Careers" name="careers" />,
    },
    {
      path: ":id",
      display: false,
      Component: () => <ViewPage group="Careers" name="careers" />,
    },
    {
      path: "apply",                       // instead of the generated `form`
      display: false,
      Component: () => <FormPage group="Careers" name="careers" />,
    },
  ],
},
```

Mix this freely with your own components: replace only the form and keep the generated list, or
wrap `ListPage` in your own layout, or add extra children the generator never produces.

#### Replacing a built-in page

```tsx
// keeps the built-in's icon, priority and permission checks
overview: { Component: MyDashboard },
```

Built-in keys: `overview`, `wallet`, `notifications`.

### Breadcrumbs from a custom page

```tsx
import { useBreadcrumbTitle } from "@/core/layouts/shared/breadcrumb"

useBreadcrumbTitle(post?.title) // sets the trailing crumb
```

---

## Layouts and Theming

Four layouts ship, selected by `VITE_APP_LAYOUT`:

| Value | Shell |
| --- | --- |
| `navbar` (default) | collapsible icon sidebar + top header with breadcrumb and actions |
| `sidebar` | classic full sidebar grouped by route group |
| `mobile` | sticky header with back/logo/actions and floating bottom tabs |
| `native` | one adaptive shell: native app on a phone, sidebar on a desktop |

All four read the same route tree, so navigation stays consistent.

#### `native`

The one to reach for when the app is going to be installed. It is a single shell that changes
shape at the `md` breakpoint rather than two layouts behind a branch:

- **Phone** — a floating translucent tab bar (first four routes plus a `More` sheet), a large
  title on each tab's own screen that becomes a compact centred title with a back button once you
  drill in, and an edge swipe that goes back with 1:1 tracking and momentum projection.
- **Desktop** — the same destinations as a persistent sidebar, a navigable breadcrumb in the
  toolbar, and the account actions in a side sheet.

Which half renders is decided by `md:` variants, not by a measured window width, so the first
painted frame is already the right size class. Safe-area insets, RTL, dark mode and
`prefers-reduced-motion` are all handled.

The platform baseline it relies on lives in `src/core/styles/index.css` and `index.html` and
applies to every layout: `env(safe-area-inset-*)` exposed as the `safe-t`/`safe-b`/`safe-l`/
`safe-r` spacing tokens (`pt-safe-t`, `pb-safe-b`, `mb-safe-b`, and so on), a `glass` utility for
translucent chrome that falls back to opaque without `backdrop-filter` or under
`prefers-reduced-transparency`, no tap highlight, no pull-to-refresh, no input-focus zoom, and
`viewport-fit=cover` so the insets report anything at all.

### How a layout is selected

There are two registries. `src/core/layouts/registry.ts` holds the built-ins and is replaced on
every sync; `src/overrides/layouts.ts` is yours and is not. `VITE_APP_LAYOUT` is looked up in
yours first, then in the built-ins, so a layout of yours named `navbar` takes over the built-in
one without you renaming it across your env files.

Both registries map a name onto a function that **loads** a layout rather than onto the layout
itself:

```ts
// src/core/layouts/registry.ts — core-owned
export const coreLayouts = {
  navbar: () => import("./navbar"),
  sidebar: () => import("./sidebar"),
  mobile: () => import("./mobile"),
  native: () => import("./native"),
}
```

Only the selected layout is ever requested, so every layout after the first costs nothing in the
initial bundle. The loader body has to be a literal `import("...")` with a static path — a
bundler cannot split a path it has to compute at runtime.

An unknown `VITE_APP_LAYOUT` is not a white screen: the app comes up on `navbar` and logs which
names are registered.

### Adding your own layout

A layout is a component that renders `children`. Put the file anywhere outside `src/core/` and
export it as `default` or as a named `Layout` — either is picked up.

```tsx
// src/layouts/compact.tsx
export default function CompactLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex h-dvh">
      <aside className="w-56 border-e">{/* your nav */}</aside>
      <main className="flex-1 overflow-auto p-4">{children}</main>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```ts
// src/overrides/layouts.ts
import type { TLayoutsOverride } from "@/core/types"

export const layouts: TLayoutsOverride = {
  compact: () => import("@/layouts/compact"),
  brand: () => import("@/layouts/brand"),
}
```

```bash
VITE_APP_LAYOUT=compact
```

That is the whole registration. Inside the layout, read the route tree with
`getNavRoutes(useLayout().router.routes)`.

Copy `src/core/layouts/{navbar,sidebar,mobile,native}/index.tsx` as starting points. `native/` is
the one to copy for a hybrid build; it already has the gesture, safe-area and size-class handling
worked out.

#### Choosing in code instead

`LayoutProvider` still takes a `layout` prop, and `src/App.tsx` is yours. Passing it skips the
registry and the lazy load entirely, which is what you want when the decision is made in code
rather than in an env file:

```tsx
<LayoutProvider router={router} layout={CompactLayout}>
  <Outlet />
</LayoutProvider>
```

### Theme tokens

- `src/index.css` is **yours**: OKLCH colour variables under `:root` and `.dark`, radii, and the
  font stacks (`--font-sans`, `--font-heading`). Restyling means editing tokens here.
- `src/core/styles/index.css` is **core's**: mechanics only — `@property` declarations,
  keyframes, scroll-mask utilities, safe-area spacing tokens, the `glass` material and the
  hybrid platform baseline. No colour tokens.

That split is the model for the whole ownership boundary: restyle freely, core still ships new
utilities, neither side loses work on sync.

Dark mode is the `dark` class on `<html>`, driven by `ThemeProvider` with `light` / `dark` /
`system` and a `localStorage` key of `theme`. Theme and direction are applied **before first
paint** by an inline script in `index.html`, so there is no flash.

`src/core/styles/fonts.css` bundles Inter (body), Geist (headings) and Cairo (Arabic). Each
`@font-face` carries a `unicode-range`, so Latin uses Inter/Geist and Arabic resolves to Cairo
per character. Fonts are bundled, not fetched, so they work offline on mobile.

> `src/index.css` contains a deliberate `@source inline(...)` block that force-generates grid and
> gap utilities, because `className` and `groupClassName` can arrive from a backend schema at
> runtime where Tailwind's scanner cannot see them. **Do not remove it**; extend the ranges if a
> schema needs a value outside them.

---

## Internationalisation

Languages `en` and `ar`, with full RTL. Detection order: `localStorage` (`i18nextLng`), then the
browser's language. Fallback `en`.

Two layers, merged in `src/i18n.ts`:

```ts
translation: { ...coreTranslations, ...appTranslations }
```

`src/core/locals/{en,ar}/` holds Thunder UI's own strings (227 keys) and is replaced on sync, so
translation fixes arrive with updates. `src/locals/{en,ar}/` is yours and starts empty. Because
the app layer merges last, **redefining a key there overrides the core string** — that is the
supported way to reword Thunder UI's text.

Schema-driven labels go through `t()` too: a field's `label`, or its name when there is no label,
is looked up — so module and field names are translatable by adding those keys.

---

## Integrations

### Triggers — notifications

Notifications are served by **Triggers** — a separate notification service, itself built with
Thunder Framework but deployed independently and not part of the framework core. It is not the
main API, and it is configured with its own base URL and tenant:

```bash
VITE_TRIGGERS_BASE_URL=https://triggers.example.com
VITE_TRIGGERS_TENANT_ID=...
VITE_UNREAD_COUNT_INTERVAL=30000   # milliseconds
```

Both the base URL and the tenant id are required for any notification UI to appear, and the
whole feature is additionally gated by `VITE_ENABLE_NOTIFICATIONS`.

What ships: a navbar popover, a mobile side sheet, and a full notifications page, plus a polled
unread count. `src/core/endpoints/notification.ts` holds the client; `useUnreadCount(userId)` in
`src/core/hooks/useUnreadCount.ts` is the polling hook. These requests send no credentials.

Push notifications on native are registered through `@capacitor/push-notifications`, and the
device token is posted to the backend with `ThunderSDK.users.addFcmToken`.

### ImageKit — uploads and image transforms

File uploads go to **ImageKit**. The browser never holds an ImageKit key: the SDK mints a
short-lived signature with `ThunderSDK.imageKit.auth()`, and `@imagekit/react` uploads directly
from the browser.

```ts
import { handleUpload, transformImage } from "@/core/lib/utils"

// Upload a file. Returns the ImageKit response, including `url`.
const res = await handleUpload(file, {
  folder: "invoices",            // defaults to VITE_UPLOAD_FOLDER
  path: ["2026", "q1"],          // optional path prefix
  filename: "custom-name.pdf",   // defaults to file.name
  signal: controller.signal,     // cancellable
  onProgress: (pct) => setProgress(pct),
})

// Request a resized variant via ImageKit's `tr` query parameter.
const thumb = transformImage(res.url, { width: 64, height: 64 })
```

Schema fields with `fieldHint: "avatar"` or `"upload"` use this automatically — the avatar
uploader and the file-table uploader both call `handleUpload` and store the returned URL.

```bash
VITE_UPLOAD_FOLDER=   # ImageKit folder; empty uses the account default
```

---

## Authentication and Multi-tenancy

Two strategies, chosen by whether `VITE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` is set:

| Mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| **OIDC** | `oidc-client-ts`. Redirect flow on web; in-app browser with a custom-scheme callback (`<appId>://auth/callback`) on native, tokens in Capacitor Preferences. |
| **Cookie session** | The default when no client id is set. Checks `/auth/api/get-session`; sign-in and sign-out go to `/auth`. |

After authentication, `ThunderSDK.plugins.essentials.registerPermissions()` runs before the app
renders — that is what makes `ThunderSDK.isPermitted()` reliable for route visibility.

The `:tenant` URL segment is pushed into the SDK. A 403 while loading permissions redirects to
the tenant picker.

---

## Mobile (Capacitor)

Capacitor 8 is pre-configured and `android/` and `ios/` are committed. The mobile build runs the
web build in `mobile` mode and then `npx cap sync`.

`capacitor.config.ts` sets `webDir: "www"`. Plugins installed: app, browser, camera, clipboard,
keyboard, preferences, push-notifications, share, splash-screen, and Android edge-to-edge.

Handled by core: status and navigation bar colours follow the resolved theme; safe-area insets in
the mobile layout; OIDC via in-app browser.

> `capacitor.config.ts` ships with `appId: "com.huruf.thunderui"` and `appName: "thunder-ui"`,
> and the committed native projects carry that identifier. **A real app must change these.** The
> visible app name comes from the `name` field in `package.json`.

---

## Environment Variables

All must be prefixed `VITE_`. `.env.example` is the canonical annotated list. Every value is a
string; boolean flags go through `envFlag()` in `src/core/lib/utils.ts`, which treats `0`,
`false`, `off` and `no` as disabled, and unset or empty as the default (`false`).

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | Backend base URL. Defaults to `window.location.origin`. |
| `VITE_OAUTH_SERVER_URL` | OIDC issuer |
| `VITE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` | Set → OIDC. Empty → cookie session. **Chooses the auth strategy.** |
| `VITE_OAUTH_SCOPE` | e.g. `full_access offline_access` |
| `VITE_APP_LAYOUT` | `navbar` (default) \| `sidebar` \| `mobile` \| `native`, or any name in `src/overrides/layouts.ts` |
| `VITE_DEFAULT_PAGINATION_LIMIT` | Page size for the card list view |
| `VITE_DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL` | SDK cache stale time, in **seconds**. Falls back to `1`. |
| `VITE_ENABLE_WALLET` | Wallet route + navbar balance widget |
| `VITE_ENABLE_USERS` | Built-in users card view |
| `VITE_ENABLE_NOTIFICATIONS` | Notifications route, navbar bell, mobile bell |
| `VITE_DEFAULT_CURRENCY` | Fallback currency code, default `LYD` |
| `VITE_TRIGGERS_BASE_URL` | Triggers service host; required for notifications |
| `VITE_TRIGGERS_TENANT_ID` | Required for notifications |
| `VITE_UNREAD_COUNT_INTERVAL` | Poll interval in **milliseconds**, default `30000` |
| `VITE_UPLOAD_FOLDER` | ImageKit folder; empty uses the account default |

### Feature flags

`src/core/lib/features.ts` exposes `features.wallet`, `features.users` and
`features.notifications`. **All are off by default** — a generated app does not inherit wallet,
user or notification UI it did not ask for.

> These replace an older `VITE_DISABLE_WALLET`, which ran the opposite way. A project that relied
> on the wallet being on by default now needs `VITE_ENABLE_WALLET=1`.

---

## Built-in Pages

| Page | Flag |
| --- | --- |
| Overview — placeholder landing page; replace via `overrides/routes.tsx` | — |
| Tenant select — tenant picker and creation form | — |
| Wallet — balance, transfer, receive via QR, currency swap, ledger, PDF export | `VITE_ENABLE_WALLET` |
| Notifications — popover, mobile sheet, full page, polled unread count | `VITE_ENABLE_NOTIFICATIONS` |
| Users — card view with ban and overdraft-limit actions | `VITE_ENABLE_USERS` |
| Not found — 404 | — |

**Onboarding.** `src/components/onboarding.tsx` is a first-launch carousel shipping with an
**empty** screen list, so nothing shows. Add entries to its `Screens` array to enable it.

---

## Verify With The Framework Team

**Do not invent any of these.** They live in the framework's tooling, not this repository.

1. For `deno task generate:sdk -v <latest-version> --overwrite`: where `<latest-version>` comes
   from — is it chosen by the developer, or read from the backend's config?
2. Which directory Thunder actually serves the UI from (`public/app/www`?), and whether the
   committed build output is what gets served in production or a build runs at deploy time.
3. How to run Triggers locally for development, since it is a separate deployment.

## Suggested Documentation Outline

If asked to write documentation for Thunder UI, these pages cover it:

| Page | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Introduction | what it generates, and that it is otherwise a normal React app |
| Installation | [Installation](#installation) |
| Updating | [Two Kinds of Update](#two-kinds-of-update) — SDK regeneration vs core sync, and the read-only rule |
| Project structure | [Project Structure](#project-structure) |
| Building your own features | [It Is Still a Normal React App](#it-is-still-a-normal-react-app) |
| How CRUD screens are generated | [How CRUD Screens Are Generated](#how-crud-screens-are-generated) |
| Shaping the UI from the backend | [Controlling the UI From the Backend Schema](#controlling-the-ui-from-the-backend-schema) — the `.meta()` reference. Arguably the most important page. |
| Schema reference | [Schema to Form Fields](#schema-to-form-fields) |
| Customization | [Customization](#customization) — one page per registry |
| Layouts and theming | [Layouts and Theming](#layouts-and-theming) |
| Internationalisation | [Internationalisation](#internationalisation) |
| Integrations | [Integrations](#integrations) — Triggers and ImageKit |
| Authentication | [Authentication and Multi-tenancy](#authentication-and-multi-tenancy) |
| Mobile build | [Mobile (Capacitor)](#mobile-capacitor) |
| Configuration | [Environment Variables](#environment-variables) |

**Tone.** Write for a developer who has a working Thunder Framework backend and wants a UI for
it. Lead every customization page with the file to edit. State the `src/core/` read-only rule
before any customization instruction. Prefer a short code sample over description. Do not imply
the developer is limited to the CRUD generator.
